misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented binomial slips from examiner reports: leaving out nCr and giving one order only (challenge tags noC, practice p1 distractor), using nPr (10P5 trap tile and prediction), writing p × r for p^r (0.25 × 5 tile), swapping the powers (swap tag, m6), the edge slip 1 − P(X ≤ k) for P(X ≥ k) (prediction, shading step miss messages, edge tag, p3 and m8), taking np as a probability (times tag) and thinking the middle score n/2 is most likely (prediction '5 right, half of them').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagbinp computes binomial probabilities: toggling four shots to collect the six orders of two hits, multiplying each order's chances, building the pmf from typed tiles with nPr, p×r and (1 − p)^n traps, reading B(10, 0.25) bars and shading cumulative events. flagbfit (when the model fits), flagpasc (Pascal's triangle), flagperm (counting) and flagpdist (general distributions) use different mechanisms, and the 30% shingle gate passed against every lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The formula is discovered before it is stated: counting the orders by hand produces 6 = 4C2, tapping each order shows all six give 0.0441 so the count multiplies one product, and the build step only accepts the three factors that match those two findings. The chart then shows that the most likely score sits near np = 2.5, and shading forces the learner to decide whether the end value is inside the event before the complement appears.

predictions.evidence: Five locked predictions with tempting wrong options: '4 orders' or '8 orders' for two hits in four, 'In, in, miss, miss' being more likely than an alternating order, '10P5 = 30240' for counting orders, '5 right, half of them' for the most likely guessing score, and '1 − P(X ≤ 3)' for at least 3. The task straight after each one tests that exact choice, and A.reveal quotes the guess in the done message.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating challenge questions with tagged wrong answers and their own corrections: noC and ratio (one order only, or a proportion instead of a probability), dice and shots (both are binomial; drawing cards without replacement is not), q and times (P(X = 0) is 0.7⁸; np is a mean), edge and flip (which side of the cut-off), swap and noC (powers and the missing coefficient). Lab slips name the error, e.g. '"More than 4" does not include 4. Start at 5.'

readability.evidence: Kid text measures FK 1.0 against the learner limit of 6.5, with one worked example (70% shooter, 4 shots) carried through every paragraph. Adult text measures FK 7.2 against the 9.5 limit while naming binomial distribution, X ~ B(n, p), binomial coefficient nCr, cumulative probability P(X ≤ r), complement and mean np. Every number is shown to 4 decimal places in the lab so learners can match their calculator.

no_filler.evidence: The filler gate passed and overlap with When a binomial model fits, Pascal's triangle and binomial coefficients, Probability distributions and Permutations and combinations stays under the 12% gate. The adult text points to the model-fit lesson rather than repeating its conditions. Each kid paragraph does one job: one order, all orders, the general rule, cumulative events.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px Android screenshots in light and dark: the four shot tiles sit across the top at about 80 px each, found orders stack two across, formula tiles wrap to two rows of three, the 11 bars each get a full-height tap column about 29 px wide plus a button twin per bar, wrapped headings stay inside the canvas, and the chosen bar's value prints under the heading instead of over neighbouring bars.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark on desktop and iPhone 13, no console or page errors, and every Show me finished in time. Each canvas action has a labelled button twin (Switch shot 1, now in; Place tile ¹⁰C₅; Bar for 5 right; Shade 3 right; Check the shaded bars), and the canvas aria-label speaks each result, e.g. 'At least 3 right = 1 − P(X ≤ 2) = 0.4744.'
